key_insight: Introduce a unified spatio-temporal token scoring mechanism that identifies and prunes redundant visual tokens across both space and time, enabling efficient video vision-language models while preserving task-relevant information.
problem_solved: Reduces excessive compute and temporal redundancy in video VLMs by jointly determining which spatial patches and temporal frames are essential for downstream vision-language tasks, instead of pruning independently in the ViT or LLM.
method: Compute unified importance scores for tokens that combine spatial and temporal cues, producing a single relevance measure per patch across frames.
Apply adaptive pruning based on those scores to discard redundant tokens early, with gating that preserves tokens critical to downstream vision-language objectives.
Integrate the scoring/pruning pipeline into the video VLM so pruning decisions are informed by end-task supervision rather than unimodal heuristics.
impact: Makes video VLMs substantially more compute- and latency-efficient with minimal performance loss, enabling scalable deployment for real-time and large-scale multimodal applications.
